entries.block: only writes session memo entries inside SignerSoftwareBase.getHdCredential
entries.reason: Constrains where a decrypted HD credential may be memoized: this is the only check that fails when a new CLI production file starts calling secureCache.set or sessionCache.set. Tests that run the code only cover the call sites that exist today, so they cannot see a write added elsewhere. Replace with a static check over the built CLI bundle.

entries.block: does not import axios, secureCache, or getHdCredential
entries.reason: get-address must stay a pure vault read: no network (axios), no session cache write, no seed access (getHdCredential). That is a property of the module's whole reachable graph, not of any one call, so no invocation of the command can demonstrate the absence of those imports. Replace with a static import-graph check over the built CLI bundle, which would also cover transitive reintroduction.

entries.block: %s keeps resource calls JSON-safe without a global codec
entries.reason: On iOS, Android and the extension, main and bg are isolated JS runtimes and hardware resources cross between them as JSON. Reintroducing jpegRgbaUtils or offscreenApiBinaryCodec anywhere on that path breaks the crossing, and absence from a module graph is not observable from any single call. Replace with a static import-graph check over the bg bundle.

entries.block: keeps the adapter SDK out of the runtime import graph
entries.reason: thirdPartyDeviceUtils ships in every platform's main bundle, and a runtime import of @onekeyfe/hwk-trezor-adapter would drag in hwk-trezor-core (~620KB). The parity test in the same file imports that SDK on purpose, so the import graph under test cannot be observed from inside this runtime. Replace with a static import-graph check over the main bundle.
